note: Recast from the description of the new species by Torales & Fontes (2008), original in English (with a Spanish abstract); the original describes the soldier and the worker but not the alate; figures 1—11 (soldier), 12—17 (heads of the two kinds of soldier) and 18—27 (worker and digestive tract) are not translated.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule yellow, speckled all over with faint dark mottling; in dorsal view the frontal gland area in front of the fontanelle is distinctly paler, whitish yellow. Postclypeus yellow, the median longitudinal line almost indiscernible. Antenna and postmentum pale yellow. Labrum yellow, the apical third paler. Mandible base brownish yellow, mandibular plate brown. The rest of the body yellowish white. Head capsule, postclypeus and labrum with scattered long erect bristles; the shorter erect bristles (shorter than the width of an antennal segment) are denser and spaced farther apart than their own length. Postclypeus with sparse microtrichia. Pronotum, mesonotum and metanotum, abdominal tergites and sternites with numerous moderately long (about equal to the width of an antennal segment) erect bristles, spaced at distances equal to or shorter than their length. The pronotum also bears long bristles near the margins; the mesonotum, metanotum and abdominal tergites have an irregular row of long erect bristles near the posterior margin. Legs with long and short erect bristles; the posterior margin of the tibia with 6—10 stout erect bristles. Tibial spur formula 3:2:2; the outer margin of the mesotibia with 2 subapical spurs; in 1 paratype soldier the outer margin of the hind tibia has an additional minute subapical spur. Head capsule (dorsal view) nearly rectangular, width about half the length, slightly wider at the mandible base; posterior angles broadly convex; posterior margin straight to very weakly concave. On the frons (in front of the fontanelle) each side bears a small but distinct warty protuberance, easily recognised when the head is viewed frontally. The frons between the two protuberances is slightly depressed, its cuticle with fine distinct wrinkles and dull; the cuticle of the rest of the head capsule is finely shagreened, nearly smooth and distinctly shining. Postclypeus about half as long as wide, sloping at about 45°, anterior and posterior margins convex, median line distinct; cuticle wrinkled and dull, as on the frons between the protuberances. Labrum nearly rectangular, anterior margin broadly convex, lateral angles rounded. Postmentum elongate, widest in the apical third. Mandibles stout, slightly curved apically; the outer margin convex in the apical third and nearly straight on the basal two-thirds; each mandible with one distinct pointed marginal tooth directed backwards. Antenna 13 segments; segment 2 about as long as 6; segment 3 narrower and shorter than the others, the remaining segments gradually lengthening towards the antennal apex. Pronotum more than 2 times as wide as long; lateral angles sharply rounded; anterior margin rounded with a shallow median notch; posterior margin broadly rounded with an almost indiscernible median notch. Abdomen slender, much longer than wide. Measurements of 2 soldiers (holotype/paratype): body length 4.25—4.50 mm, head length (lateral view, to the lateral mandible base) 1.40 mm, head length (to the apex of the postclypeus) 1.50—1.45 mm, head width 1.05—0.97 mm, head depth (excluding the postmentum) 0.70—0.73 mm, postclypeus length 0.25—0.20 mm, postclypeus width 0.50 mm, postmentum length 0.65—0.66 mm, postmentum width 0.30 mm, pronotum length 0.25—0.26 mm, pronotum width 0.60—0.65 mm, left mandible length 0.73—0.75 mm, left mandible width at the apical tooth 0.10—0.13 mm.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head yellow, the rest of the body white; abdominal sclerites transparent, the gut contents visible through them. Head with numerous moderately long (about equal to the width of an antennal segment) erect bristles and scattered short bristles. The disc of the pronotum with moderately long erect bristles, the margins with longer erect bristles. Abdominal tergites and sternites with numerous moderately long erect bristles. Lateral margins of the head almost parallel in the anterior two-thirds, narrowing posteriorly in the posterior third; posterior margin broadly rounded. Postclypeus moderately inflated, slightly shorter than half its width. Antenna 13 segments; segment 2 about equal to segments 3 and 4 together, segments 3 and 4 the narrowest; the remaining segments gradually widening and enlarging towards the apex. Pronotum similar to that of the soldier, but without a median notch on the anterior and posterior margins. Abdomen slender, much longer than wide. Digestive tract: gizzard anterior, dorsolateral on the left side of the abdomen; mixed segment extending from the middle of the right side to the ventral surface of the abdomen, its end reaching the sagittal line; enteric valve posterior, dorsolateral on the left side of the abdomen. Measurements of 2 workers: head length (to the apex of the postclypeus) 0.73—0.85 mm, head width 0.80—0.90 mm, postclypeus length 0.15—0.23 mm, postclypeus width 0.40—0.46 mm, pronotum length 0.20 mm, pronotum width 0.50—0.55 mm, abdomen length 2.15—2.70 mm, abdomen width 0.90—1.20 mm.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The soldier is easily distinguished from O. brevicorniger: the soldier of the latter has a darker and smaller head capsule, no warty protuberances on the frons, a wrinkle-free frons cuticle, a postclypeus sloping at only 30°, and more strongly curved mandibles. As for the worker, O. brevicorniger is larger and slightly darker, with the head widest anteriorly in dorsal view and somewhat trapezoidal.
